# KOVA Lifestyle — Digital Marketing Launch

A separate digital marketing portfolio project by Mahima Mahajan. KOVA is a fictional Indian T-shirt brand. Operations Studio remains a different project about business processes.

## Campaign brief

Campaign: **Wear your everyday.**

The first-drop idea combines Everyday and Oversized fit concepts for men and women with Ink, Chalk and Sage. Proposed product prices are ₹699 and ₹899, consistent with the separate Operations Studio example. There are no real garments, verified fit measurements or products for sale.

Proposed audience: adults aged 18–30 in India, including students and people early in their careers who want simple casual outfits. No interviews or audience survey were conducted. These audience descriptions are hypotheses.

Positioning to test: make everyday outfit choice easier with a short collection, clear fit explanation and styling ideas. No tested quality, sustainability, ethical-production or delivery claim is made.

Primary planning goal: 60 expressions of interest in 30 days, using an illustrative ₹12,000 media budget and a target ₹200 cost per lead. This is a goal, not a benchmark, forecast or result. A real qualified lead would require a valid, consented signup, relevant delivery location and expressed interest in the product. The demo does not collect that information and cannot produce qualified leads.

## The journey

1. Introduce the idea through original social creative and proposed prospecting ads.
2. Help interested people compare fits through the carousel, article and product concept page.
3. Bring commercial search intent to the same landing page with clearly grouped search ads.
4. Demonstrate a signup and a success state without sending or storing an email.
5. Use the local event log to test the journey, then inspect a separately labelled synthetic reporting example.

## Deliverables

- 11 finished campaign designs: 3 feed posts, 5 carousel slides and 3 stories, each in editable SVG and 1080-pixel-wide PNG format.
- 30 proposed content days with headline, caption, CTA, format, goal and asset reference.
- 3 reel storyboards with hooks, shot timing, voiceover and CTA. These are scripts, not filmed videos.
- 3 Google Search ad groups with 15 headline assets and 4 description assets each: 57 text assets in total.
- 30 keyword ideas with intent, use, proposed match type and destination page. 29 are commercial ideas and 1 is informational. No volume or search-position data is claimed.
- 15 negative keyword ideas to review before actual setup.
- A Meta prospecting test plan comparing fit-led and colour-led concepts, plus a conditional retargeting plan.
- A separate interactive landing page, original fit article and 4 rendered email drafts.
- A UTM builder, event definition and QA plan, local browser event log, synthetic funnel CSV and scenario calculator.
- 2 original AI-generated source images and the prompts used to create them.

## Why these choices

### Research and limitations

Public pages reviewed on **30 October 2026**:

1. [Bewakoof oversized T-shirts](https://www.bewakoof.com/oversized-t-shirts) displayed men’s and women’s products, fit labels, ratings, sale prices and product filters. Decision: make fit and product choice clear without trying to match a large catalogue. This is an inference, not a conversion finding.
2. [Bonkers Corner homepage](https://www.bonkerscorner.com/) displayed collection names, collaboration links, men’s and women’s categories and promotional messages. Decision: give KOVA one recognisable launch theme and a simple route to the first drop. This is an inferred creative direction, not evidence of an unmet market need.

No competitor performance, customer data, keyword volumes or demand estimates were obtained. The public pages can change after the observation date.

### Google Search

Budget proposal: ₹6,000 over 30 days, or an illustrative ₹200 daily allocation. Ad groups: Everyday men, Everyday women and Oversized. Exact and phrase matches are proposed starting points. Match behaviour, exclusions, location settings and conversion configuration need review inside a real account.

Assets were checked against the limits in [Google’s responsive search ad guidance](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7684791?hl=en): 30 characters per headline and 90 per description, with up to 15 and 4 assets respectively. Character compliance does not mean policy approval, ad strength or actual delivery has been verified.

No search campaign, platform account, bid strategy, keyword forecast or billing setup was created. The small budget is a planning scenario and could be insufficient for a meaningful real experiment.

### Meta

Budget proposal: ₹6,000 over 30 days. Prospecting starts as a broad-audience hypothesis with serviceable Indian locations to be confirmed. The proposed A/B test changes only the creative angle: fit first versus colour first. Hold dates, audience, placements, offer, page and budget constant. Compare cost per qualified lead and landing-page lead rate, not clicks alone.

The protocol is a draft. No randomised experiment, sample-size calculation, significance result, configured campaign or available retargeting audience is claimed. Retargeting would only be considered after eligible, consented traffic exists, with lead exclusions and frequency review.

### SEO and email

The article answers a fit question rather than inventing product evidence. The landing page and article have descriptive titles, meta descriptions, a single H1, internal links and alt text. No structured product availability, fake review schema or ranking result is included.

The four emails are welcome, preview, launch and a future-store cart draft. They are standalone HTML copy/layout examples. There is no list, email provider or automation. Cart recovery requires a real saved basket, appropriate consent and purchase suppression before it can be implemented.

## Measurement: three distinct categories

### Planned

₹12,000 budget, 30 days, 60 interest leads and target ₹200 CPL are proposed planning inputs.

### Synthetic example

| Channel | Spend | Impressions | Clicks | Landing sessions | Leads |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Google Search | ₹6,000 | 20,000 | 600 | 510 | 30 |
| Meta prospecting | ₹6,000 | 60,000 | 600 | 480 | 24 |
| Total | ₹12,000 | 80,000 | 1,200 | 990 | 54 |

Derived values: total CPL ₹222.22, click-to-session rate 82.5%, session-to-lead rate about 5.45%. Search CTR is 3%, Meta CTR is 1%. Search CPL is ₹200 and Meta CPL is ₹250. The synthetic example misses the goal by 6 leads. No purchases or revenue are inferred.

What to practise: check landing-page delivery, message match, fit questions and form completion before proposing the next test. These invented numbers cannot justify a real channel budget change or a claim of marketing success.

### Local QA activity

The landing page records page_view, view_item, select_content and generate_lead in localStorage for this browser only. The names follow a proposed plan informed by [GA4 recommended events](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/9267735?hl=en), but GA4 is not installed.

The log stores event names, timestamps, selected concept products and allowlisted UTM values. It does not store email. The demo form discards the email and never sends it. There is no server lead store, ad pixel, analytics request or real subscription. Up to 100 local events are retained and the visitor can clear them.

Before a real launch: establish consent/privacy handling, validate events in the chosen analytics property, confirm deduplication, keep personal information out of events and URLs, define qualified leads and verify conversion import before media spending.

## AI assistance and authorship

ChatGPT and Codex assisted with research summaries, campaign planning, copy, original image generation, vector layouts, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, local event logic, calculations and verification. Do not claim these assets were created entirely without AI. Images show fictional models and product concepts, not actual customers or verified garments.

## Portfolio scope

This project demonstrates an integrated marketing plan and working prototype. It does not demonstrate paid-campaign management, delivered email automation, ranking growth, real customer acquisition or live commercial outcomes. BookNest has not been deleted or modified.
